title: The Lord Who Measured Zero
chapter: Chapter 4: The Knight in the Snowdrift

lines.text: Twenty lamps. Tobin could make one every two days, if Ash kept bringing rimeglass. Forty days. We had sixty. For the first time since the Measuring, the numbers were on my side.
Naturally, that was when a knight fell off his horse at our gate.
My lord! There's a man in the snowdrift. He's either dead, or very drunk.
Very drunk, as it turned out. A steel breastplate, a good sword, and a smell that made the goats leave.
Sir Oswin Hale. Formerly of the King's Third Company. Formerly of a lot of things. Is this the edge of the world?
Close. It's Greyhollow.
Same thing.
I know that name, my lord. Hale was stripped of his spurs last year. They say he refused an order.
What order?
To burn a village that couldn't pay its taxes. With the villagers still inside.
Nobody said anything for a while.
We could use a man who knows how to fight. The pay is terrible. The roof is half finished. Breakfast is mostly goat.
You're offering me a post? I'm a disgrace.
I'm a zero. We'll get along fine.
He stayed. On the first day, he slept. On the second, he trained Wren. On the third, he trained everyone.
Again! Shield up, Tobin! You hit like a man apologising!
By the end of the week, Oswin had stopped drinking. He said the cold air cleared his head.
I found out much later that he'd told Bram his sword arm felt ten years younger. And that Bram had told him to keep it to himself.
Meanwhile, the lamps piled up. Seven. Eight. Nine. Pell's sleigh would be back within the month.
On the night of the ninth lamp, the grain store caught fire.
Fire! The grain store's on fire!
We formed a line from the stream. Buckets, pots, anything that held water. Ash dragged sacks out of the flames with his teeth.
We saved the building. We lost half the grain. Half of everything we had to eat until spring.
This was no accident, my lord. Someone poured lamp oil along the back wall. I can still smell it.
In the snow behind the store, Wren found boot prints. Southern boots, heading for the road.
That night I sat alone with the ledger. Half the grain. Thirty-seven mouths. Ninety days of winter.
And for the first time since I arrived, I felt the cold. Truly felt it. Deep in my bones, as if something I couldn't see had been hurt.
Somewhere to the south, someone was smiling. I intended to ruin their day.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter five, coming soon.
